title: Every task adds to one visible piece
statement: Make every small task visibly add to one artifact the learner is building, such as a paragraph that fills as they work, so no step feels like a separate task.
example: In one prototype, three quote break-down conversations finished and left no artifact.
detail: A review of a Grade 9 lesson prototype named a lot of little tasks that never came together as its most persistent finding across two units, and traced it to tasks that end without producing anything the learner can see. It set as a rule that every small task should visibly be part of one thing being built. In its rebuild of independent practice the paragraph fills as the learner works and stays visible throughout, which it names as what makes the small tasks cohere. The prototype's modelled-paragraph screen, which visibly builds a paragraph, was already the working case.

evidence.quote: This pass identifies the mechanism: tasks end without producing anything the child can see.
Every small task should visibly be part of one thing being built. If a step produces nothing the child can point at, it will feel like a task rather than part of a lesson, however good the step is.
The paragraph fills as the student works, and is visible throughout. This is what makes the small tasks cohere.
